reviewBoundary: Two complete new junior3 fifteen-gap four-choice cloze narratives. Context and all alternatives checked by the author, with candidate presentation shuffled before freezing. No claim of independent teacher review, learner calibration or source-paper text reuse.

materials.title: The first village tour
materials.text:
Before guiding visitors on our village open day, I memorised dates, names and facts about the old mill. At home, I could deliver my speech without a ____1____.

My first visitors were a family from abroad. I spoke quickly so I would not ____2____ anything. The father raised his hand. Instead of asking about history, he wanted somewhere to ____3____ water.

My speech contained nothing about shops. Mei, another volunteer, pointed to a cafe. The family asked to go there before ____4____ the tour.

While they bought drinks, Mei asked what I wanted them to remember. "Everything," I replied. She looked at my thick pages and ____5____.

"Could you choose three things?"

I chose the mill, bridge and a tree planted by the first schoolchildren. For each, I selected one ____6____ instead of many dates.

When the family returned, we walked more ____7____, allowing time for photographs. The children asked why the mill wheel no longer turned. Answering was easier while we were ____8____ beside it.

The mother thanked me for the stories. I had told much ____9____ than planned, but the family had joined the conversation.

I kept my research for when I needed to ____10____ a detail. I simply stopped treating every fact as something I must ____11____ immediately. A tour was not an examination of my ____12____; it helped people notice a place. Mei had made me more ____13____ to the people beside me, without making me less prepared.

For the next group, I began with a ____14____: "What would you most like to see?" Then I ____15____ to the answer.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The memorised speech can be delivered without a pause. Tickets and maps are tour resources, and without a visitor does not describe fluent rehearsal as specifically as pause.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The narrator speaks quickly to avoid forgetting memorised material. Selling, borrowing and repairing do not describe retaining a speech.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The later cafe visit and bought drinks establish buying water. Measuring or hiding it is not their need, and carry concerns transport rather than obtaining a drink.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: They take a drink break before continuing the interrupted guided walk. Cancelling would end it, selling is unrelated and printing is not part of the walk.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Mei responds gently with a practical suggestion, fitting smiled. She remains present and awake, and no disagreement or quarrel is described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The narrator chooses a story for each site instead of dates, confirmed by the mother enjoying stories. Price, number and address are isolated facts rather than the narrative focus.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Leaving time to look and photograph means walking slowly. Nervousness and secrecy are not the new approach, and carelessness contradicts attention to visitors.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Standing beside the wheel gives a shared visible reference for the explanation. Hiding or sleeping contradicts active guiding, and no cooking takes place.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Choosing only three stories means telling less than the planned exhaustive account. Faster reverses slowing down; loudness and lateness are not the contrast.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Retained research lets the narrator check details. Inventing contradicts researched accuracy, while hiding and selling do not explain its continuing usefulness.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The narrator no longer must repeat every researched fact at once. Translating, protecting and losing do not express exhaustive delivery to visitors.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: Memorised historical facts test knowledge. Speed was a delivery problem, not the subject being examined; clothes and age are unrelated.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Adapting to visitors makes the guide attentive to them. Fame, similarity and distance do not capture responsiveness.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The quoted request for preferences is a question. It is neither a warning, promise nor joke.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Responding to visitor preferences starts by listening to their answer. Returning, dancing and pointing do not express receiving the answer.

units.title: The notes I did not play

materials.title: The notes I did not play
materials.text:
Joining the school orchestra as a percussion player, I wanted everyone to hear me. My part contained a few notes separated by long ____1____, when I was meant to make no sound.

At rehearsal, I counted the empty bars, then struck the drum as ____2____ as possible. The conductor stopped us.

"You entered at the right moment, but listen around you."

I was confused. I had made no ____3____ in counting. What else mattered?

We began again without my drum. I heard a quiet flute phrase above the strings. My loud beat had ____4____ its ending. My timing was right, but my volume was wrong.

Next time, I played more ____5____. The flute remained clear. My note could ____6____ another instrument instead of compete with it.

The silent bars were no longer a gap before my ____7____. They were music I needed to hear before deciding how to play.

At the concert, I dropped a drumstick between pieces. I felt embarrassed, but retrieved it during the ____8____ without interrupting anyone.

My brother barely noticed. He remembered the music, not the stick. I had expected every ____9____ to attract attention. In fact, I was part of something much ____10____.

I still practise counting: timing ____11____. But I practise listening too. A correct note is not automatically a ____12____ contribution if it covers another phrase. Participation includes knowing when to be ____13____. I no longer need my part to be the ____14____ sound. I want it to help the whole piece ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The following explanation defines rests as times with no sound. Seats, songs and meals do not name silent musical intervals.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Wanting to be heard and later being told the volume was wrong establishes loudly. Late contradicts correct timing; slowly concerns rhythm and quietly conflicts with drowning the flute.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Made no mistake in counting expresses the belief that timing was correct. Choice, promise and change do not name the error being denied.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The loud beat covers the flute ending, later contrasted with keeping it clear. Following, inventing and measuring do not describe masking sound.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Reducing volume means softly. Anger, frequency and carelessness do not solve the masking problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: A small supporting weight works beneath the flute. Replace and silence remove its role; copy duplicates rather than complements it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The player had treated silence as waiting for their own turn. Lesson, chair and record do not describe the next opportunity to play.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Between pieces, a pause permits retrieving the stick without interruption. Argument and meal are absent, while melody implies active playing rather than the available break.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The dropped stick is an error the narrator fears everyone will notice. Recipe, seat and page do not name the mishap being discussed.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Being one part of a larger ensemble puts the accident in perspective. Quieter is not the scale comparison, and price/age do not express the whole-versus-part relation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Continued counting practice shows accurate timing matters. Vanishes contradicts retaining it; changes and waits do not explain why accuracy remains important.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: A note that masks another phrase is not a helpful contribution. Silent contradicts the audible note; private and regular do not assess its effect on the ensemble.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Musical participation includes silence and listening, so quiet. Absence means not being there, fame is irrelevant, and being first concerns sequence rather than restraint.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The opening desire to be heard is replaced by not needing to be loudest. Nearest and latest concern position/time; smallest is not the status initially sought.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The aim is making the whole piece work musically. Disappear and wait prevent performance; compete introduces the rivalry the player has moved beyond.
